source.supports: validateId(id, name) rejects non-numbers, non-integers and values at or below zero. Its name argument only shapes the message, so every identifier in the API shares one domain; it is applied at 129 call sites.

probe.note: A public method taking a single identifier, used to prove this domain against the driver rather than against an internal validator the package does not export.

positive_id.semantics: No coercion. The validated number is passed positionally and appears verbatim in the request path.

requirements.description: Preserve the value at its explicit driver argument and wire location.
Accept a representative positive integer.
Reject a representative invalid value before driver invocation.
Reject a missing required input.
Accept the largest safe integer, which is the largest value that can round-trip through JSON.

Reject a value above the largest safe integer. The driver accepts it, because it checks Number.isInteger rather than Number.isSafeInteger, so this is an MCP boundary check: a value that cannot round-trip through JSON would address a different record than the caller named.
Where the identifier is optional, omit it entirely when the caller did not supply it rather than sending a default; a required identifier drops this requirement at resolution.

source.supports: validatePaginationParams rejects a limit that is not a positive integer, and one above the documented maximum of 250.

probe.note: The public page helper carries limit and offset, so the domain is proven where the driver actually applies it.

pagination_limit.semantics: No coercion. Sent as a path-style query control, never as a JSON body field.

requirements.description: Preserve the value at its explicit driver argument and wire location.
Accept a representative page size.
Reject a representative invalid page size before driver invocation.
When omitted, send the adapter's page default of 50 explicitly rather than leaving TestRail to choose, so the page returned is the page the metadata describes.
Accept the documented maximum page size.
Reject a page size above the documented maximum rather than letting the server silently clamp it.

source.supports: validatePaginationParams rejects an offset that is not a non-negative integer. Zero is valid and means the first page.

probe.note: The public page helper carries limit and offset, so the domain is proven where the driver actually applies it.

pagination_offset.semantics: No coercion. Zero is a meaningful value and is not treated as absent.

requirements.description: Preserve the value at its explicit driver argument and wire location.
Accept a representative offset.
Reject a representative invalid offset before driver invocation.
When omitted, send offset 0 explicitly so the first page is requested by name rather than by default.
Accept an explicit zero offset as the first page rather than discarding it as a falsy value.

source.supports: resolveCollectionOptions validates pageSize as a positive integer not exceeding 250 before the first request, and defaults it to 250.

probe.note: The public aggregate helper carries every bound, so each is proven where the driver applies it rather than against the page helper's separate validator.

aggregate_page_size.semantics: All mode only. Forwarded as the driver's pageSize when supplied; the driver's own default of 250 applies when omitted, and the adapter does not invent one.

requirements.description: Preserve the value as the pageSize option of the aggregate helper.
Accept a representative page size.
Accept the documented maximum page size.
Reject a non-positive page size before driver invocation.
Reject a page size above the documented maximum rather than letting the server clamp it.
Forward no pageSize when the caller did not supply one.

source.supports: resolveCollectionOptions validates startOffset as a non-negative safe integer before the first request, defaults it to 0, and requires the first envelope's offset to equal it.

probe.note: The public aggregate helper carries every bound, so each is proven where the driver applies it.

aggregate_start_offset.semantics: All mode only. Forwarded as the driver's startOffset when supplied; the aggregate starts at 0 when omitted. Zero is a meaningful value and is not treated as absent.

requirements.description: Preserve the value as the startOffset option of the aggregate helper.
Accept a representative starting offset.
Forward an explicit zero rather than discarding it as a falsy value.
Reject a negative or non-integer offset before driver invocation.
Forward no startOffset when the caller did not supply one.

source.supports: resolveCollectionOptions validates maxItems as a positive safe integer before the first request and defaults it to 25,000. The adapter's aggregateLimitDefaults (src/contracts/inputs.ts) caps what a caller may request at 1,000, and DEFAULT_LIMITS forwards 1,000 when the caller sets none.

probe.note: The public aggregate helper carries every bound. A value above the adapter ceiling is accepted by the driver, which is why that rejection is recorded as the adapter's.

aggregate_max_items.semantics: All mode only. Forwarded verbatim when supplied; the configured limit (1,000 by default) is forwarded when omitted, so an aggregate never runs under the driver's own default. The ceiling the schema enforces is the built-in default, not the operator's configured value.

requirements.description: Preserve the value as the maxItems option of the aggregate helper.
Accept a representative bound.
Accept the configured ceiling itself.
Reject a non-positive bound before driver invocation.
Reject a bound above the configured ceiling rather than letting a caller raise the operator's limit.
Forward the configured limit when the caller did not supply one.

source.supports: resolveCollectionOptions validates maxPages as a positive safe integer before the first request and defaults it to 100. The adapter's aggregateLimitDefaults caps what a caller may request at 20, and DEFAULT_LIMITS forwards 20 when the caller sets none.

probe.note: The public aggregate helper carries every bound. A value above the adapter ceiling is accepted by the driver.

aggregate_max_pages.semantics: All mode only. Forwarded verbatim when supplied; the configured limit (20 by default) is forwarded when omitted, so an aggregate never runs under the driver's own default.

requirements.description: Preserve the value as the maxPages option of the aggregate helper.
Accept a representative bound.
Accept the configured ceiling itself.
Reject a non-positive bound before driver invocation.
Reject a bound above the configured ceiling.
Forward the configured limit when the caller did not supply one.

source.supports: resolveCollectionOptions validates maxBytes as a positive safe integer not exceeding 1 GiB before the first request and defaults it to 100 MiB. The adapter's aggregateLimitDefaults caps what a caller may request at 1 MiB, and DEFAULT_LIMITS forwards 1 MiB when the caller sets none.

probe.note: The public aggregate helper carries every bound. A value above the adapter ceiling is accepted by the driver.

aggregate_max_bytes.semantics: All mode only. Forwarded verbatim when supplied; the configured limit (1 MiB by default) is forwarded when omitted, so an aggregate never runs under the driver's own default. Bounds the UTF-8 bytes of the serialized items.

requirements.description: Preserve the value as the maxBytes option of the aggregate helper.
Accept a representative bound.
Accept the configured ceiling itself.
Reject a non-positive bound before driver invocation.
Reject a bound above the configured ceiling.
Forward the configured limit when the caller did not supply one.

source.supports: resolveCollectionOptions validates maxDurationMs as a positive safe integer not exceeding five minutes before the first request and defaults it to five minutes. The adapter's aggregateLimitDefaults caps what a caller may request at 45,000 ms, and DEFAULT_LIMITS forwards 45,000 when the caller sets none.

probe.note: The public aggregate helper carries every bound. A value above the adapter ceiling is accepted by the driver.

aggregate_max_duration_ms.semantics: All mode only. Forwarded verbatim when supplied; the configured limit (45,000 ms by default) is forwarded when omitted, so an aggregate never runs under the driver's own default. Bounds the aggregate's wall-clock time.

requirements.description: Preserve the value as the maxDurationMs option of the aggregate helper.
Accept a representative bound.
Accept the configured ceiling itself.
Reject a non-positive bound before driver invocation.
Reject a bound above the configured ceiling.
Forward the configured limit when the caller did not supply one.

source.supports: serializeIdFilter(value, name) accepts one identifier or an array of them, validates each member with validateId, joins an array with commas, and returns undefined for an empty array so the filter is omitted from the request.

probe.note: The public page helper carries every case filter; the domain is proven through typeId, one of the seven filters the driver serializes this way.

id_filter.semantics: One identifier or a non-empty list. A list is sent comma-joined under the filter's REST name. An empty list is refused at the boundary: the driver would omit the filter, silently widening the result to every case.

requirements.description: Preserve the value at its explicit driver argument and wire location.
Accept a representative single identifier.
Accept several identifiers and send them comma-joined.
Accept the largest safe integer, which is the largest value that can round-trip through JSON.
Reject a representative invalid value or list member before driver invocation.
Reject a value above the largest safe integer, alone or as a member. The driver checks Number.isInteger only, so this is an MCP boundary check.
Reject an empty list rather than letting the driver drop the filter.
Omit the filter entirely when the caller did not supply it rather than sending a default.

source.supports: The get_cases preparation forwards createdAfter, createdBefore, updatedAfter and updatedBefore to the query unchanged and applies no validation to them, so their domain is held entirely at the MCP boundary.

probe.note: Proven through createdAfter. The driver accepts every invalid value below, which the library records rather than implies.

unix_timestamp.semantics: Seconds since the Unix epoch, as TestRail documents its timestamp filters. No coercion; zero is the epoch and is sent.

requirements.description: Preserve the value at its explicit driver argument and wire location.
Accept a representative timestamp.
Accept zero, the epoch, and send it rather than treating it as absent.
Accept the largest safe integer, which is the largest value that can round-trip through JSON.
Reject a negative, fractional or string value before driver invocation; the driver would forward each of them.
Reject a value above the largest safe integer, which cannot round-trip through JSON.
Omit the filter entirely when the caller did not supply it rather than sending a default.

source.supports: getCaseTitles refuses an empty list and validates every member with validateId before joining them with commas. The bulk case payload schemas declare case_ids as an array of numbers and forward it unchecked; the MCP boundary holds each member to the identifier domain and requires at least one.

probe.note: The public title lookup takes the list positionally and validates it the way the bulk endpoints need, so it proves the domain without a payload. A body reference records in its semantics that the driver itself forwards the payload unchecked.

case_ids.semantics: A non-empty list of case identifiers. Sent comma-joined as a query control by get_case_titles and as a JSON array in every bulk body.

requirements.description: Preserve every member at the explicit driver argument and wire location.
Accept a representative list of identifiers.
Accept a member equal to the largest safe integer.
Reject a list with a non-positive, fractional or string member, or a value that is not a list, before driver invocation.
Reject a member above the largest safe integer. The driver checks Number.isInteger only, so this is an MCP boundary check.
Reject an empty list; there is nothing to act on and TestRail answers 400.
Reject a missing list.
